title: Vanishing from finite submodules by filtered colimits
statement: Let $h:Y\to X$ be a quasi-compact quasi-separated morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], $q\in\mathbf Z$, and $M$ a module over the universe lift of $\mathbf Z$. Let $n\in\mathbf N\setminus\{0\}$ annihilate every element of $M$. Write $\underline N$ for the constant module sheaf on the small etale site of $Y$ attached to a submodule $N\subseteq M$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves, def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. If $R^q h_*\underline N=0$ for every finite submodule $N$, then $R^q h_*\underline M=0$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. The submodule index may live in the universe of $M$.

proof.text: Index the inclusion diagram by finitely generated submodules of M. The zero submodule gives nonemptiness and the sum of two finitely generated submodules gives directedness. Every element is in its cyclic submodule, so compatible maps glue uniquely and the diagram has colimit M. A k-generated submodule killed by nonzero n is a quotient of (Z/n)^k, so is finite. Constant sheafification preserves this colimit.

For q nonnegative compute higher direct image from the sheafified presheaf of cohomology on pullbacks of affine etale objects. The pullbacks are qcqs. Apply the coherent-site filtered-colimit cohomology argument of Tag 0739, in the lifted universe containing the submodule index. Its proof uses finite covers, so needs no restriction to Type 0. Pullback and sheafification preserve colimits. Hence the higher image of the union is the filtered colimit of the higher images of its constant finite submodules. The existing Type-0 Lean preservation interface is not enough by specialization alone; generalize its finite-cover proof to this universe.

All terms in this last diagram are zero, so its colimit is zero. For negative q the derived pushforward of a sheaf in degree zero is concentrated in nonnegative degrees, giving vanishing directly. M=0 and n=1 are included.
